title: Memory is application data with a lifetime
outcome: Choose what to retain, revalidate, summarize, and delete between agent steps and sessions.
cue: Memory needs a purpose, a scope, and an expiry.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Choose what to retain, revalidate, summarize, and delete between agent steps and sessions.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: Memory can preserve stale facts and injected instructions. Summarization can reduce size while increasing ambiguity.

trace.title: Current intent
trace.detail:
## Understand

Short-term context is what the current request sees. Durable application state can include conversations, task progress, user preferences, evidence snapshots, tool outcomes and pending approvals.

These stores are not the model's weights.

Retain only what serves a purpose. A summary can lose an exception, change an uncertain statement into a fact, or preserve a malicious instruction.

Keep source IDs and confidence/status labels with summaries. Treat stored memories as outside data on future turns.

A memory key must include the relevant identity and scope. Recheck current access before reusing records or facts.

A user's old permission does not authorize today's retrieval. Define retention, correction and deletion across derived caches and summaries.

Product memory should not grow forever merely because storage is cheap.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail:
Current request → relevant permitted history → task state → bounded evidence → model call → explicit durable updates. Simulate a scope change and access revocation before a later turn.

Check what is invalidated or reloaded.
